text:
sasha: quick q — reproducible bug when streaming from RN WebView: initial request with ephemeral token works, then when we rotate token (refresh) the WebView starts returning CORS errors: 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' missing and the stream halts. static long-lived token works fine. anyone seen this with WKWebView / Android WebView + streaming?

raj: yes — common RN/webview cookie/SameSite trap. if you're relying on Set-Cookie for the rotated token, WebView might block it. recommended: send rotated token in Authorization header and reconnect the stream. for streaming, you can do a short reconnect with new header.

maya: can you paste the error log? is it a preflight (OPTIONS) failing or a fetch rejection? CORS errors often show in the console before the 401. also check server sends the CORS header on the preflight too (not just 200 responses).

sasha: console shows CORS + then 401 in server logs. sequence: 1) client opens EventSource -> ok, 2) token expires, client POSTs /refresh -> gets new token (we set cookie via Set-Cookie), 3) we send postMessage to webview to update creds -> try to resume stream -> browser rejects with CORS.

kevin: two gotchas: (1) iOS WKWebView blocks third-party cookies frequently and Set-Cookie may be ignored unless SameSite=None and Secure and proper third-party context; (2) EventSource / SSE can't update headers mid-stream — you must reopen. suggested flow: don't rely on cookies in the WebView. instead: pass ephemeral token to the WebView via the JS bridge and use fetch/WebSocket with Authorization header. example for injecting header in RN WebView JS:

```js
// inside injected JS
window.openStream = (token) => {
  const es = new EventSource('/v1/stream?access_token=' + encodeURIComponent(token));
  // OR use a small fetch + websocket that sets Authorization header
}
```

or better: expose a native method to set header on the WebSocket client in Swift/Kotlin wrapper if you're using native streaming.

raj: another approach: if you must use cookies, ensure backend responds to OPTIONS with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to the exact origin (not '*'), and client uses withCredentials. but RN WebView still flaky.

mobile-ci-bot: docs: https://redwood.example.com/docs/mobile-auth — section "WebView token rotation" has patterns for header injection and reconnects. :book: 

maya: quick question for SDK folks — for native Swift/Kotlin wrappers, do we have a helper to swap tokens and reattach KV cache / resume stream without losing state? would simplify client logic.

kevin: not yet; current pattern is: short-lived tokens + automatic reconnect with idempotent resume token in query param (stream_resume_id). on reconnect server rewinds to last acked event. we can add a helper in the mobile SDK to do the reconnect+auth dance. filing a tiny RFC would help.

sasha: great — will try sending Authorization header via bridge and do reconnect. i'll upload logs if still failing. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
